answer: To achieve Sybil resistance within an autonomous agent network, the protocol forces nodes to anchor their cryptographic identities to non-fungible hardware roots of trust and stake economic collateral. At the dawn of each consensus epoch, the network evaluates an identity graph, pruning malicious clusters. An attacker seeking to flood the ecosystem must deploy an exponentially scaling capital commitment to spawn even a small grove of valid identities, rendering large-scale identity spoofing economically irrational.
